title: Protocol to identify and analyze mouse and human quiescent hematopoietic stem cells using flow cytometry combined with confocal imaging
protocol: Harvest bone marrow from mouse hind leg bones.
Remove large muscles and clean bones of remaining tissue.
Rinse bones with 2% FBS/PBS solution to remove any attached hair.
Place cleaned bones in buffer on ice.
Transfer bones to a biosafety cabinet for sterile conditions.
Harvest BM using flushing approach.
Cut off only a thin piece of epiphysis at the end of the bone.
Hold the bone shaft with forceps.
Insert a 23-gauge needle attached to a syringe into the end of the bone.
Completely flush BM into a 15 mL conical tube using no less than 3 mL (per mouse) 2% FBS/PBS.
Flush multiple times until bone shafts turn white.
Gently pipette flushed BM up and down using a 1 mL micropipette to disperse BM aggregates.
Wash the cells with an additional 3 mL of 2% FBS/PBS by spinning down at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Crush bones briefly using a mortar and pestle in a small volume of 2% FBS/PBS just enough to cover the bones.
Add approximately 10 mL 2% FBS/PBS to the crushed bones.
Swirl around to gently release BM from bone fragments.
Pipette up and down to disperse BM aggregates using a 10 mL pipette.
Pass the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer placed in a 50 mL conical tube to remove bone debris.
Add 10 mL of 2% FBS/PBS to the mortar.
Collect bone marrow (BM) cells as specified.
Repeat until suspension becomes clear and colorless.
Centrifuge BM cell suspension at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend BM cells in 2 mL of 1× BD Pharm Lyse buffer.
Incubate RBC lysed BM cells for 3 minutes in a 37°C water bath or 15 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge the incubated suspension at 300 g for 5 min.
Wash the pellet once with at least 10 mL of 2% FBS/PBS.
Resuspend RBC lysed BM cells in 2 mL of 2% FBS/PBS.
Filter the resuspended cells through a 40 μm cell strainer into a 5 mL FACS tube.
Take 5 μL and make a 200-fold dilution for counting total number of cells.
Adjust the final cell concentration to 1 × 10^8 cells/mL in up to 2 mL volume.
Save an aliquot of 1.5 × 10^6 cells for FACS controls.
Perform lineage depletion using the EasySep Mouse Hematopoietic Progenitor Cell Isolation Kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Count the number of isolated cells after lineage depletion.
Resuspend Lin- BM cells at a concentration of 1 × 10^7 cells/mL in 2% FBS/PBS for immunostaining.
Resuspend ∼1 × 10^6 total BM in 100 μL of 2% FBS/PBS for immunostaining.
Label three FACS tubes as TMRE, DAPI, and unstained.
Transfer ∼10^4 total BM to each of the three labeled tubes.
Add 200 μL of 2% FBS/PBS to the tubes labeled as unstained and DAPI.
Prepare four tubes of UltraComp Plus compensation beads, labeling them for CD48-APCCy7, Sca-1-PB, c-Kit-APC, and CD150-PECy7.
Vortex UltraComp Plus compensation beads thoroughly.
Add one droplet to each tube containing the labeled compensation beads.
Add 1 μL of corresponding antibody as labeled on the tube.
Protect the tubes from light.
Use 1 μL antibody per 1 × 10^6 cells per 100 μL for mouse HSCs.
For every 1 × 10^7/mL Lin- BM cells, add 2 μL Streptavidin-APCCy7 (SA-APCCy7) and 10 μL each of the following antibodies: anti CD48-APCCy7, Sca-1-PB, c-Kit-APC, CD150-PECy7.
Mix well and incubate for 20 min on ice. Protect from light.
Wash cells with 2% FBS/PBS by centrifuging at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant quickly by tilting once.
While keeping the tube inverted, aspirate off the last hanging droplet to remove all the supernatant.
Proceed to TMRE staining.
Add 1 μL Anti CD48-APCCy7 antibody and 0.5 μL SA-APCCy7 to 100 μL of 10^6 total BM cells.
Mix well and incubate for 20 min on ice. Protect from light.
Wash the cells with 2% FBS/PBS by centrifuging at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant quickly by tilting once.
Do not remove the last droplet.
Place cells on ice and protect from light.
Prepare 2 mL of 100 nM TMRE staining medium in 10% FBS/IMDM pre-warmed at 37°C.
Resuspend full stain sample cell pellet and cells from the tube marked as TMRE, each in ∼500 μL pre-warmed TMRE staining medium.
Incubate for 15 min at 37°C in humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2.
Wash with 2% FBS/PBS by centrifuging at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant without aspirating the last hanging droplet, leaving ∼200 μL in the tube.
Add 2% FBS/PBS to the above ∼200 μL cell suspension to reach 1 × 10^7/mL for DAPI staining of full stain sample (Lin- BM).
Add 1 μL of 1 mg/mL DAPI to 1 mL of full stain sample.
Filter through a Falcon cell strainer cap into a 5 mL FACS tube.
Add 2 μL of 100× DAPI staining solution into ∼200 μL cells in the tube for DAPI single staining control.
Add 2 μL of 100× DAPI staining solution into ∼200 μL cells in each tube for Lin/CD48-APCCy7 positive staining control (total BM).
Set the temperature of the sample injection chamber to 4°C for sorting distinct MMP fractions of CD48-LSK CD150+ HSCs.
Make plots over FSC/SSC, FSC-A/FSC-H, SSC-A/SSC-H, DAPI, APCCy7, APC/PB, PECy7.
Draw tentative gates on each plot starting with the Debris gate (FSC-A/SSC-A).
Proceed to the doublet gate using FSC-A/FSC-H.
Continue by setting another doublet gate using SSC-A/SSC-H.
Set the DAPI gate next.
Follow with the APCCy7 gate.
Then set the APC+PB+ gate.
Lastly, set the PECy7+ gate.
Adjust the voltage for each parameter accordingly.
Load the full stain sample (Lin- BM).
Acquire events to reveal populations in all gates.
Remove the tube once voltages are set and place it on ice.
Set compensation using single staining controls with unstained samples.
Compensate using DAPI-stained samples.
Compensate using TMRE-stained samples.
Compensate using CD48-APCCy7 antibody-stained samples.
Compensate using Sca-PB antibody-stained samples.
Compensate using cKit-APC antibody-stained samples.
Compensate using CD150-PECy7 antibody-stained samples.
Calculate spill over matrix and apply compensation to all samples.
Determine the Lin-CD48- gate by acquiring a Lin/CD48 positive staining control (total BM).
Set the Lin-CD48- gate according to the clear-cut bottom edge of the APCCy7-positive population, ensuring no more than 1% falls into the negative gate.
Determine the Lin-CD48- gate.
Flow cytometry contour plots for total bone marrow (Lin/CD48) staining control and Lin-enriched bone marrow full stain sample.
Gating scheme towards CD48-LSKCD150+ from Lin-enriched mouse bone marrow.
Gate debris- cells.
Gate doublets-.
Gate DAPI- single viable cells.
Sequentially gate Lin-CD48- bone marrow (Gate 1).
Determine Sca-1+c-Kit+ gate (Gate 2) on a plot of APC against PB under Lin-CD48- gate (Gate 1).
Set Sca-1+c-Kit+ gate to include the most positive population.
Acquire at least 100,000 to 200,000 fully stained Lin- bone marrow sample.
Determine CD150+ gate on a plot of PECy7 under Sca-1+c-Kit+ gate to include the most positive population.
Plot TMRE histogram from 100 CD150+ HSCs.
Gate top and bottom most 25% as MMP-High and MMP-Low.
Sort MMP-Low and -High HSCs into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes containing 200 μL cold StemSpan.
Monitor the TMRE profile during sorting on the FACS sorter.
Re-adjust MMP-Low and -High gates if necessary when multiple tubes are used for samples with large volume.
Divide large sample volumes into multiple tubes and keep the remaining samples on ice.
Ensure a reliable TMRE profile based on sufficient cell numbers for real-time MMP gate adjustment.
Display at least 50,000 Lin- BM cells per screen refresh to ensure the display of more than 50 CD160+ HSCs.
Set Events to Display to maximum using BD FACSDiVa software.
Take a proportion of pooled BM equivalent to the amount of one bone for analysis.
Perform RBC lysis, lineage depletion and immunofluorescent staining of Full Stain Sample and controls as described in 2.a. – 3.b.
Resuspend washed Full Stain Lin- BM in 1.5 mL pre-warmed 10% FBS/IMDM.
Divide the cell suspension into 3 FACS tubes, 500 μL each.
Mark the tubes as NT (non-treated), CCCP, or Oligomycin.
Add 5 μL of 10 mM CCCP stock to 500 μL cell suspension marked as CCCP for a final concentration of 100 μM.
Add 5 μL DMSO each to 500 μL cell suspension marked as NT or oligomycin.
Incubate the tubes for 10 min at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2.
Prepare 20 μL of 10 μM TMRE (1:10 diluted from 100 μM working stock) in 10% FBS/IMDM.
Add 5 μL of 10 μM TMRE into each of 500 μL cell suspensions.
Return cells to the incubator for another 15 minutes.
Prepare a 25 μL working stock of 200 μg/mL Oligomycin in 10% FBS/IMDM.
Add 5 μL of 200 μg/mL Oligomycin into 500 μL cell suspension labeled as oligomycin to achieve a final concentration of 2 μg/mL, 5 minutes before the end of incubation.
Return cells to the incubator and incubate for an additional 5 minutes.
Immediately fill tubes with ice cold 2% FBS/PBS after incubation ends.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant, leaving ∼200 μL in each tube.
Add 2 μL of 100× DAPI staining solution into the remaining cell suspension.
Keep cells on ice and protect from light for flow cytometry analysis.
Isolate human mononuclear cells (MNCs) from peripheral blood (PB).
Obtain fresh, non-mobilized whole PB from normal donors from NY blood center.
Disinfect blood pouches with 70% ethanol and wipe them down.
Disinfect the tubing on the pouches using alcohol prep pads in a biological safety cabinet.
Enrich CD34+ MNCs through immunomagnetic column separation.
Stain live cells with HSC specific immunofluorescent antibodies.
Label cells with mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) specific probe TMRE.
Sort distinct MMP fractions of CD34+CD38-CD45RA-CD90+ Human HSCs using flow cytometric sorter.
Cut open the tubing using a clean, disinfected razor blade.
Release blood into 50 mL conical tubes or other sterile containers.
Dilute whole blood at least 1:1 with 1 × PBS.
Add 15 mL Ficoll-Paque PLUS in each 50 mL conical tube.
Layer approximately 30 mL of diluted blood on the Ficoll-Paque PLUS.
Tilt the tube as low as possible toward the bench top.
Gently release the diluted blood using a 25 mL pipette.
Allow the blood to flow slowly over the Ficoll surface.
Set the centrifuge brake to “off” or adjust deceleration to the minimum level.
Centrifuge the blood-Ficoll mixture at 800 g for 30 minutes at 18°C–20°C.
Carefully separate the bottom red blood cell pellet layer (∼7.5 mL).
Collect the middle colorless Ficoll layer containing granulocytes (∼15 mL).
Gather the top yellow and clear plasma layer containing platelets (∼25–30 mL).
Harvest the white, thin ring of mononuclear cells (MNCs) between the Ficoll and plasma layers.
Vacuum aspirate off most of the upper plasma layer without disturbing MNC layer, leaving approximately 5 mL above.
Insert a 10 mL pipette through the remaining plasma layer and collect the entire MNC layer.
Pool collected MNC suspensions into 3–4 new 50 mL tubes.
Set the centrifuge brake back to “on” or deceleration to maximum level.
Centrifuge pooled MNC suspensions at 300 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove most supernatant without disturbing pellets, leaving approximately 5 mL.
Resuspend pellets with remaining supernatant.
Pool all MNC suspensions into one tube.
Thoroughly rinse off any remaining cells in all tubes with small amount of 2% FBS/PBS and combine the rinse-off with pooled MNC suspension.
Centrifuge again at 300 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Mix well after filling up the tube to 50 ml with buffer.
Take 5 μL, dilute 1:20, and count the number of cells if the pellet appears slimy or slushy.
Cryopreserve an aliquot of 5 × 10^6 or 1 × 10^7 MNCs in freezing buffer at -80°C (short term) or liquid nitrogen (long term).
Isolate CD34+ cells from PB MNCs.
Centrifuge MNCs at 300 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove most of the supernatant, leaving a thin layer unstirred.
Add 1 mL MACS buffer to resuspend the pellet.
Adjust the final volume to approximately 1.4 mL per 1 × 10^9 cells with additional MACS buffer if needed.
Add 300 μL FcR blocking reagent to every 1.4 mL cell suspension.
Subsequently add 300 μL microbeads from CD34 MicroBead kit to the cell suspension, making the total volume ∼2 mL at 5 × 10^8 cells/mL.
Determine CD90+CD45RA- gate using flow cytometry contour plots of FITC vs. PECy7.
Gate debris- in the sample.
Gate doublets- in the sample.
Gate DAPI- cells in the sample.
Sequentially gate for CD34+ (Gate 1), CD38- (Gate 2), and CD45RA-CD90+ (Gate 3) from CD34+ enriched PB MNCs.
Set bottom 25% MMP-Low and top 25% MMP-High gates in the TMRE flow histogram of CD34+CD38-CD45RA-CD90+ HSCs.
Insert an LS column into the separator.
Place a collection tube underneath the column.
Apply 2 mL MACS buffer to the column reservoir and let it run through to rinse the LS columns.
Resuspend the cell pellet in approximately 5 mL MACS buffer to a concentration of around 1 × 10^8 cells/500 μL.
Filter the resuspended cells through a Falcon cell strainer to remove clumps larger than 30 μm.
Pass the filtered cells through the LS column.
Wash the LS column twice with 5 mL MACS buffer after all the cells are processed.
Wait for the column to empty completely before adding the buffer.
Remove the column from the separator and place it over a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 5 mL MACS buffer into the column.
Push the plunger into the column and elute the magnetically labeled cells.
Count the number of eluted CD34+ MNCs without dilution.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 g for 10 min to pellet the cells.
Resuspend the cells in freezing buffer.
Cryopreserve aliquots at 1 × 10^6 or 5 × 10^5 cells/vial in liquid nitrogen (>1 month) or at -80°C (<1 month).
Thaw one vial of 0.5 × 10^6 or 1 × 10^6 CD34+ MNCs and one vial of 1 × 10^6 MNCs.
Gently transfer cells to 20 mL 2% PBS/FBS buffer in a biosafety cabinet.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min.
Carefully aspirate off most supernatant without stirring up cell pellet, leaving about 1 mL at the bottom.
Resuspend cells and filter through a 40 μm cell strainer cap into 5 mL FACS tubes.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Aspirate off most supernatant of CD34+ MNCs, leaving ∼200 μL.
Transfer 200 μL MNCs to each of the following FACS tubes: FMO (CD38-PerCPCy5.5), FMO (CD90-FITC).
Label 3 FACS tubes as TMRE, DAPI, and unstained.
Transfer 30 μL of remaining MNCs to each labeled tube.
Prepare four tubes of UltraComp PLUS beads, labeling them CD34-APC, CD38-PerCP-Cy5.5, CD90-FITC, and CD45RA-PECy7.
Vortex UltraComp PLUS compensation beads thoroughly.
Add one droplet of beads to each labeled tube.
Add 1 μL of the respective antibody to each tube containing beads.
Label tubes as TMRE, DAPI, or unstained for single staining controls (probes).
Mix antibodies with cells according to manufacturer’s instruction: Add 5 μL anti-CD34-APC, 5 μL anti-CD38-PerCP-Cy5.5, and 10 μL anti-CD90-FITC to CD34+ MNCs.
Add 5 μL anti-CD34-APC, 10 μL anti-CD90-FITC, and 5 μL anti-CD45RA-PECy7 for FMO (CD38-PerCP-Cy5.5) staining control.
Mix 5 μL anti-CD34-APC, 5 μL anti-CD38-PerCP-Cy5.5, and 5 μL anti-CD45RA-PECy7 for FMO (CD90-FITC) staining control.
Keep all tubes on ice and protect from light.
Mix well and incubate on ice for 20 minutes, protected from light.
Fill FACS tubes with 2% FBS/PBS and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant quickly in one smooth motion.
While the tubes are in the inverted position, aspirate off the last hanging droplet.
Prepare 2 mL of 100 nM TMRE staining medium in 10% FBS/IMDM pre-warmed at 37°C.
Resuspend full stain sample, both of FMO staining controls, and TMRE-single staining control, each in approximately 500 μL pre-warmed TMRE staining medium.
Incubate at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2 for 15 minutes.
Fill the FACS tubes with 2% FBS/PBS and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate off most of the supernatant, leaving approximately 200 μL for FMO gating controls or TMRE staining control, and approximately 500 μL for CD34+ cells.
Resuspend the remaining two single staining controls (DAPI, unstained) in 200 μL 2% FBS/PBS.
Prepare 20 μL of 100× DAPI staining solution.
Add 2 μL of 100× DAPI staining solution in each of the two 200 μL FMO controls and DAPI-single staining control.
Add 5 μL of 100× DAPI to 500 μL of CD34+ cells.
Sort distinct MMP fractions of CD90+ HSCs (CD34+CD38-CD45RA-CD90+ HSCs) using a 5 laser BD FACSAria sorter with a 100 μm nozzle and 4-way purity sorting mode.
Set the temperature of the sample injection chamber to 4°C.
Make plots over FSC/SSC, FSC-A/FSC-H, SSC-A/SSC-H, DAPI, APC, PerCPCy5.5, FITC/PECy7.

Draw tentative gates subsequently on each of the plots in the following order: Debris gate (FSC-A/SSC-A), doublet gate (FSC -A/-H), doublet gate (SSC -A/-H), DAPI gate, APC+ gate, PerCPCy5.5- gate, FITC+PECy7- gate.
Set voltage for each of the parameters.
Load the full stain sample (CD34+ MNCs).
Acquire just enough events to reveal population in all gates.
Adjust the voltages to appropriate ranges for each parameter.
Remove the tube once the voltages are set and place it on ice.
Set compensation.
Acquire the following single staining controls: unstained, DAPI, TMRE, CD34-APC, CD38-PerCPCy5.5, CD90-FITC, CD45RA-PECy7.
Calculate spill overs and apply compensation matrix to all.
Set the gates for CD90+ HSCs (CD34+CD38-CD45RA-CD90+ Human HSCs).
Acquire FMO (CD38-PerCPCy5.5) for CD38- gating reference.
Acquire FMO (CD90-FITC) for CD90+ gating reference.
Acquire at least 20,000 cells of FMO staining control with CD38-PerCPCy5.5.
Determine the CD38- gate using the differential expression of CD38 within the CD34- population as a reference.
Adjust the CD38- gate on a plot of PerCPCy5.5 against APC based on clear separation between positive and negative populations.
Verify that the CD38- gate comprises 90%–95% CD34+ cells using FMO (CD38) staining control.
If quantity is prioritized over purity, set the CD38- gate at the bottom edge of the positive CD38 population.
If purity is prioritized over quantity, apply a more stringent CD38- gating by setting the gate at the top edge of the negative CD38 population.
Determine the CD90+CD45RA- gate on a plot of FITC against PECy7.
Acquire minimal sufficient number (3,000–5,000 cells) of fully stained CD34+ PB MNCs.
Sort MMP-Low and MMP-High HSCs into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes containing 200 μL cold StemSpan.
Wait until a stable TMRE profile is shown before determining MMP gates.
Monitor the shift of TMRE profile during sorting.
Re-adjust MMP-Low/-High gates whenever MMP-low gate comprises more than 30% and MMP-high gate less than 20% of the entire profile.
Concentrate samples to under 500 μL to raise acquisition rate close to or above 100 events/second.
Sort murine HSC fractions using FACS.
Transfer 4,000–5,000 sorted cells into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Spin down the cells at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate most of the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet, leaving about 100 μL medium.
Resuspend the pellet with StemSpan/Pen Strep to a total volume of 1.5 mL.
Spin down the cells again at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate most of the supernatant, leaving about 100 μL medium in the tube.
Add StemSpan/Pen Strep to adjust the total volume slightly above 800 μL.
Gently pipette up and down to resuspend the cells.
Transfer 800 μL cell suspension to a new tube.
Add 8 μL 100 × cytokine mix to achieve final concentrations of SCF at 100 ng/mL and TPO at 20 ng/mL.
Mix well gently.
Transfer 200 μL cells from the previous step to each of the 4 wells in a U-bottom 96 well plate.
Mark the wells as DMSO, Leu (Leupeptin), ConA (Cocanamycin), and CQ (chloroquine).
Add 2 μL DMSO to one well to achieve a final concentration of 1%.
Add 2 μL of 10 mM Leupeptin stock to another well to achieve a final concentration of 100 μM.
Add 2 μL of 4 μM ConA working concentrate to another well to achieve a final concentration of 40 nM.
Add 2 μL of 4 mM chloroquine concentrated working solution to the last well to achieve a final concentration of 40 μM.
Incubate the cells at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere with 5% CO₂ for either 4 h or 18 h depending on the assay.
Harvest cells after incubation.
Transfer all harvested cells into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Rinse the plate twice with 200 μL cold StemSpan/Pen Strep (without cytokine) and collect any remaining cells.
Wash cells with cold StemSpan/Pen Strep.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate most of the supernatant without disturbing the cells, leaving about 200 μL medium.
Prepare immunofluorescence slides using Channel μ-slide technology from ibidi for minimal volume sample processing.
Replace solutions in each channel by pipetting at least 50 μL of fresh solution into the slanted channels.
Remove excess solution from the other side of the slide with a kimwipe to ensure complete replacement.
Rinse or wash the channels by pipetting 200 μL of required wash buffer, 3–5 times the volume in each channel in a slanting position and simultaneously dab off the overflow.
Pipette 50 μL fibronectin coating solution (75 μg/mL in Ca2+/Mg2+ free PBS) in each channel of the slide in a slanting position for coating ibidi μ-slides.
Incubate the coated slides at room temperature for 1 h.
Wash the slides twice by pipetting 200 μL PBS into one end of the channel in a slanting position and simultaneously dabbing off the overflow.
Thoroughly rinse off unbound fibronectin.
Store coated slides at 4°C in a sealed humidity container.
Fix cells on the slides.
Transfer 200 μL of washed cells into a 1.5 mL or 500 μL microcentrifuge tube for inhibitor treatment.
Transfer 500–1,000 freshly sorted/treated cells into a 1.5 mL or 500 μL microcentrifuge tube.
Spin down the cells at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate most of the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, leaving only 30–50 μL at the bottom.
Mix to resuspend the cells.
Pipette 30 μL of cell suspension into the channel of the slide.
Carefully insert the slide into a Cytospin clip without filter paper, facing up.
Gently fasten the clip and place in the spinner recess, balanced, tilted forward and facing down.
Spin at 200 rpm for 2 min at room temperature using medium acceleration.
Carefully remove the slides from the binder without stirring up the cells.
Incubate the slides for 30 min at 37°C with 5% CO2 in a sealed humidity container.
Prepare fresh 4% PFA from commercially available 16% PFA stock solution during incubation.
Rinse off the medium with 200 μL PBS after incubation.
Pipette at least 50 μL of freshly prepared 4% PFA into the channel in a slanting position to replace PBS.
Briefly dab off the overflow onto a tissue.
Refill the channel with 4% PFA and incubate for 15 min at ∼23°C.
Wash three times for 5 min each with 200 μL PBS.
Check under the microscope if enough cells (>40 per channel) are present on the slide.
Pipette 50 μL permeabilization buffer (0.25% Triton-X 100) into the channel and replace PBS as described in the beginning.
Fill the channel with another 50 μL permeabilization buffer.
Incubate the slide in a sealed humidity container for 15 min at ∼23°C.
Wash three times for 5 min each with 200 μL PBS.
Pipette 50 μL blocking buffer (3% BSA/PBST) into the channel and replace PBS as described previously.
Fill the channel with another 50 μL blocking buffer.
Incubate the slide in a sealed humidity container for 1 hour at approximately 23°C.
Wash the slide three times for 5 minutes each with 200 μL PBST.
Dilute rabbit anti-TOM20 and mouse anti-LAMP1 antibodies in 1% BSA/PBST (1:150).
Pipette 50 μL of the primary antibody cocktail into the channel.
Replace PBST as described previously.
Fill the channel with another 50 μL of the same primary antibody cocktail.
Incubate the slide in a sealed humidity container for 12-18 hours at 4°C.
Wash the slide three times for 5 minutes each with 200 μL PBST.
Dilute goat anti-rabbit IgG: Alexa Fluor 594 and goat anti-mouse IgG: Alexa Fluor 488 antibodies in 1% BSA/PBST (1:1,000).
Pipette 50 μL of the secondary antibody cocktail into the channel.
Replace PBST as described previously.
Fill the channel with another 50 μL of the same secondary antibody cocktail.
Incubate the slide in a sealed humidity container for 1 hour at approximately 23°C in the dark.
Wash the slide three times for 5 minutes each with 200 μL PBST in the dark.
Replace PBST with sufficient mounting medium containing DAPI.
Aspirate off any bubbles at the opening of the channel.
Fill the channel and its openings with mounting medium, avoiding any bubble formation.
Place a piece of coverslip at one edge of the slide.
Push the coverslip toward the other end without drawing in bubbles.
Dab off extra liquid briefly.
Seal the coverslip with transparent nail polish.
Allow to dry at approximately 23°C.
Store slides at 4°C.
Take images as soon as possible.
Mount the slide on the microscope.
Open Zen (black edition) software on the computer and start the system start.
Apply immersion oil to both the 40× and 100× oil immersion objectives.
Insert the channel μ-slide on the microscope stage facing up.
Position ibidi μ-slides facing up on an inverted microscope.
Locate cells using the “Locate” tab in Zen workspace software.
Switch from a 20× objective to a 40× oil immersion objective (N.A. 1.4).
Center one of the cells and then switch to a 100× oil immersion objective (N.A. 1.46).
Focus using the fine adjustment knob.
Click “Acquisition” tab in Zen workspace.
Click on “Smart Setup” and add fluorescent labels: DAPI, A488, A594 (PE Texas Red) in dye drop down menu.
Select “Best Signal” imaging option and press the “Apply” button.
Turn on excitation lasers for DAPI (Diode laser 405 nm), HeNe laser 594 nm, and Argon laser 488 nm automatically turns on.
Set parameters in the “Acquisition Mode” window from the “Acquisition Parameter” tool group.
Set scan mode to Frame.
Set frame size to 1024 × 1024.
Set scan speed to 8.
Set scan step to 1.
Set averaging number to 2.
Choose Averaging Mode as Mean or Median.
Set bit depth to 12.
Set direction to Unidirectional.
Adjust scan area to Zoom 4.
Select the channel with the longest wavelength first (A594).
Proceed with settings for one channel at a time in the "Tracks" list.
Start live preview scanning of the cell in focus.
Adjust laser power to 2% using the slider in the lasers field under the selected track.
Move the “Gain” (Master) slider between 600–800 to adjust detector sensitivity.
Monitor pixel intensity in the center screen area.
Click on “Range Indicator” in the “Dimensions” tab for a gray scale image appearance.
Identify saturated red pixels indicating high intensity areas.
Monitor the histogram of pixel intensity in the “Display” tab.
Adjust gain and laser power: Ensure no red pixels are present, signal ranges to 2/3 of the scale. Increase laser power if signal is dim at gain above 800; decrease if image is saturated below 600.
Set laser powers up to 20% or 30% for far reds with very low detector efficiency.
Click “Stop” when satisfied and record gain / laser power values.
Test a few cells across experiment groups.
Set optimal gain / laser power according to the specimen with the highest signal of a particular channel.
Switch to the next channel and repeat steps.
Adjust pinhole size based on requirements.
Select the channel of the longest wavelength for further adjustments.
Click on "1AU" in the "Pinhole" field.
Record the automatically calculated value shown in the gray box.
Input the recorded pinhole value in the gray box for all remaining channels.
Activate the “Single Channel” checkbox on the “Dimensions” tab.
Click on the icon of the channel to be adjusted.
A single channel image shows in the middle view area.
On the “Display” tab, click the icon of the channel to be adjusted.
Move the Black point and White point control beneath the histogram to adjust contrast and brightness.
Test multiple images to optimize settings.
Once optimal black/white levels are determined, click the setting icon above the histogram.
Click “Copy” in the pull-down menu.
For all images acquired, click “Paste” from the setting menu to apply the same display settings.
Note: If the icon is not visible, select the checkbox of "show all" on the top of the tab.
Open Zen (Blue edition) software.
In the “Processing” tab, press the “Batch” button.
Choose “Image Export” from the “Batch Method” pull-down menu.
Click “+ Add” and upload .czi files to be exported.
Highlight any one of the uploaded files.

Set parameters in the “Parameters” window: File Type: Tagged Image. Compression: None. Resize: 100%. Original Data: Deselect except required. Apply Display Settings and Channel Color: Select. Choose Merged Channels Image and/or Individual Channel Image. Use Full Set of Dimensions: Select.
Click “Copy Parameters” in the “Batch Processing” area.
Select all image files and click “Paste Parameters”.
Click “Run Selected” to export raw images as .tiff files.
Assign DAPI (Channel 1), A488 (Channel 2), A594 (Channel 3) to separate tracks in the SR mode.
Turn on excitation lasers: Channel 1: Diode 405, Channel 2: Argon 488, Channel 3: HeNe 594.
Open “Imaging Setup” window and set the beam path: Click on “Ch.A” checkbox in the beam path and activate the Airyscan detector.
Choose dual band path filters: BP 420–480 + BP 495–620 (Channel 1, 2, 3).
Replace mirror with a plate.
Choose Beam Splitters/dichroics: Main Visible Beam Splitter – MBS 488 (Channel 2)/594 (Channel 3).
Main UV Beam Splitter – MBS 405 (Channel 1).
Duplicate and create a total of three tracks, one for each channel.
Open “Channels” window.
Set Airyscan Mode to SR (Super Resolution) for each channel.
Set Pinhole to 3.5AU for each channel.
Set Detection gain and laser power according to confocal laser scanning microscopy imaging parameters.
Set excitation parameters that give the best signal vs. noise ratio while utilizing 50% of the full dynamic signal range and avoid saturation.
Keep detector gain below 850V to ensure linearity of the response (750V–850V is ideal for Airyscan).
Laser power for Airyscan rarely exceeds 1%.
Open “Acquisition Mode” window from “Acquisition Parameters” tool group and set the following parameters.
Acquire z-stack series of images.
Click on “z-stack” checkbox in the multidimensional input field underneath the action buttons.
Open “z-stack” window from “Multidimensional Acquisition” tool group.
Set up z-stack range using First/Last mode.
Press the “First/Last mode” button.
Click “Continuous” to keep scanning the specimen.
Turn focus control knob towards yourself until reaching the first plane in focus, top of the specimen.
Click “Set First”.
Then turning focus control in the opposite direction until reaching the last plane in focus, bottom of the specimen.
Click “Set Last”.
Once set, click “Stop”.
Press “Optimal” button to determine z-Step interval when SR mode is activated.
Choose “Airyscan Processing” in the pull down “Method” list under “Processing” tab.
In “Method Parameters” window, press “Select” button.
Click on “Auto” checkbox in “Processing Strength” area.
Press “Run Batch” button and select the files.
Click “Apply” button at the top of “Processing” tab.
Process all images in the z-stack series.
Acquire confocal microscopy images using ZEISS’ ZEN 2 Black software version 14.0.21.201 and ZEN 2.6 Blue edition.
Export acquired images for further processing.
Open .tif file of a merged channel image in ImageJ software.
Select the cell area (e.g., 160 × 160 pixel square) using a selection tool.
Copy the selected cell region to the system clipboard.
Set measurement scale by selecting Analyze > Set Scale and clicking “remove scale” to revert to pixel measurements.
Configure measurement settings by selecting Integrated Density (IntDen).
Split the color image into three grayscale images of each channel (red, green, blue) using Image > Color > Split Channels.
Convert the split images to 8-bit format.
Activate the gray image of green channel (LAMP1-Alexa Fluor 488; lysosome).
Close red (LC3-Alexa Fluor 594) and blue (DAPI) channel images.
Go to Analyze > Measure.
In the popup window, note the values of IntDen and RawIntDen.
Open the next image file.
Go to Edit > Selection > Restore Selection.
Move the frame to select the cell.
Repeat steps f-k and analyze 30–50 cell images per experiment group.
Record all values under RawIntDen as the fluorescence intensity of LAMP1.
Measure average fragment area of mitochondria.
In ImageJ, open .tif file of a merged channel image.
Use a selection tool to select the cell (e.g., 160 × 160 pixel square).
Go to Edit > Copy to System to save the selection.
Go to Analyze > Set Scale and click “remove scale” to revert to pixel measurement.
Go to Analyze > Set Measurements and select Area.
Go to Image > Color > Split Channel.
Activate the gray image of red channel (TOM20- Alexa Fluor 594; mitochondria).
Close green and blue channel images.
Go to Image > Adjust > Threshold.
Restore Selection from Edit > Selection > Restore Selection.
Move the frame to select a cell.
Analyze colocalization of mitochondria with lysosomes by determining the fraction of TOM20 accumulated in LAMP1 positive areas among total cellular TOM20 using Mander’s overlap coefficient value M1.
Measure colocalization between LC3 and LAMP1, defining M2 as the ratio of total signal intensity in one channel from pixels that also show signals above the threshold of another color channel.
Download JACoP v2.0 plugin for ImageJ from imagej.nih.gov/ij/plugins/track/jacop2.html.
Copy-paste downloaded JACoP (.jar) into Plugin folder in ImageJ.
Open merged channel images in ImageJ.
Use a selection tool to select the cell, e.g., 160 × 160 pixel square.
Go to Edit > Copy to System to save the selection.
In ImageJ, go to Analyze > Set Scale and click “remove scale” to revert to pixel measurement.
Go to Image > Color > Split Channels.
Color the gray images according to their channel color.
Go to Image > Type, choose RGB color.
Go to Image > Color > Make composite.
Open both green and red individual color images.
Go to Plugins > JACoP.
Choose an image file from drop-down list (red or green channel) for Image A or B.
Under Analysis to perform, click check M1 & M2 coefficients (Manders’ Coefficients).
Click Threshold tab at the bottom.
Threshold will be automatically set for each channel.
Click Analyze button.
Record all M1 values (using threshold).
Open a merged channel image.
Use a selection tool to select the cell (e.g., 160 × 160 pixel square).
Copy the selected area to system clipboard.
Set scale to revert to pixel measurement.
Select Integrated Density as measurements.
Split channels into individual color images.
Activate the gray image of green channel (LAMP1-Alexa Fluor 488).
Keep the red channel image (LC3-Alexa Fluor 594) open.
Close the blue channel image.
Adjust threshold settings for both LAMP1 and LC3 channels.
Select Default threshold.
Click Auto to set threshold.
Create selection from pixels within threshold.
Go to Analyze > Tools > ROI Manager.
Press Add.
Select the ROI and rename it as LAMP1.
Activate the gray image of red channel (LC3-Alexa Fluor 594).
Repeat step h-k.
Select the newly added ROI and rename it as LC3.
Select both ROIs of LAMP1 and LC3.
Click More.
Choose “And” for overlapping between LAMP1 and LC3.
Click Add.
Rename the new ROI as “coloc” (colocalization).
Select ROI “coloc” in ROI Manager.
Click activate the red channel image (LC3).
Click Measure in ROI Manager.
Record IntDen value from Results window.
Move the frame to select the cell on the next image.
Repeat steps f-v and analyze 30–50 cell images per condition per experiment.
